heroHeadline: Trump Holds Arms 'In Abeyance' as 'Negotiating Chip'; PLA at 6 Sorties Post-Summit; HIMARS Deadline 14 Days; CFR: 'Taiwan Tests US-China Ties Soon'
heroSubtitle: President Trump has confirmed the $14 billion PAC-3 MSE/NASAMS arms package is 'in abeyance' — characterizing it as a 'very good negotiating chip' with Beijing in post-summit statements that alarmed bipartisan congressional Taiwan hawks. Trump also publicly told Taiwan to 'cool it a little bit.' The Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14-15) concluded without a joint communiqué on Taiwan, no US decision on the arms package, and Xi Jinping's defining warning — 'Handle Taiwan badly and the two countries risk collision or conflict' — standing unaddressed. The Council on Foreign Relations assessed: 'Decent peace at the summit, but Taiwan tests begin now.' The Atlantic Council called Trump's summit outcomes 'underwhelming' on Taiwan. PLA maintained moderate post-summit pressure on May 17: 6 aircraft sorties (4 entering SW/Eastern ADIZ), 5 PLAN vessels + 1 official ship — down from the 15-aircraft summit-conclusion day surge (May 15) but above summit-window lows. Taiwan News analysis published May 16 identified Taiwan's NT$780B special defense budget as 'strategically incomplete' — T-Dome, domestic drone scale-up, and joint manufacturing absent. The HIMARS payment deadline (May 31) is now 14 days away; Taiwan MND is prepared to use reserve funds as backup if the legislature fails to approve timely disbursement. Full May PLA sortie sequence: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6.
